label: Flask samples
title: Extending the project into a Flask web app
summary: Three projects that move the validate → analyze → HTML flow of Week 11, Session 2 into a Flask web app: Korean stocks (sample2), US stocks (sample1) and SQLite storage (sample4). Run each as a server inside the virtual machine and send it requests with wget.

sample2_korea.summary: Korean stock analysis app. app.py receives the request, storage.py reads the CSV, logic.py validates and analyzes it, and templates/index.html (Jinja) draws the page. Check the KOSPI/KOSDAQ filter, the ranking by change, the sample mean and the 400 response to bad input.
sample2_korea.notes: On a real PC, install Flask in a virtual environment as the README says, run python app.py and open http://127.0.0.1:5002 in your browser. The virtual machine in this web lab has no network connection to the page, so a browser cannot reach its server; requests are sent from inside the machine with wget and test_client() instead.
steps: A one-day (2026-11-05) fictional snapshot of 5 stocks. Prices are whole won (KRW), and codes such as 005930 are handled as strings to keep the leading 0.
Start the development server in the background (&). Its address is http://127.0.0.1:5002 and it can only be reached from inside this virtual machine. Loading Flask takes about 10 seconds.
Wait until the server answers, then save the first page (market ALL) as page.html: 5 stocks · up 2 / down 2 / flat 1 · sample mean +0.40%.
The query string ?market=KOSPI reaches the app through request.args.get('market'). The mean of the 3 KOSPI stocks is +0.33%.
The mean of the 2 KOSDAQ stocks is +0.50%. It is an equal-weight sample mean of the selected stocks, not a market index return.
For an unknown market, analyze() raises ValueError and app.py answers 400 BAD REQUEST. wget does not show the body of an error response.
test_client() sends a request to the app without starting a server. Check the status code 400 and the error message shown on the page (market must be ALL, KOSPI or KOSDAQ).
The server log has one line per request with its path and status code (200, 200, 200, 400). test_client() requests bypass the server, so they are not here.

To view the page in your own browser, download sample2.html and style.css one at a time with the box above (into the same folder) and open sample2.html. The server's /static/ path was rewritten to the file name.
Stop the background server (job 1). On a real PC you stop it with Ctrl+C in its terminal.

sample1_us.summary: A US stock app with the same structure. Prices are stored as whole cents and converted to USD only on screen (scale=100); the markets are NASDAQ/NYSE and codes are uppercase tickers. Compare it with sample2.
steps: A price of 22000 is $220.00. Amounts are stored as whole cents to avoid floating-point errors.
The only differences between the two apps are in logic.py: the market list (MARKETS) and the code check (six digits ↔ uppercase ticker). The rest of the flow is the same.
Start the server on port 5001.
ALL: 5 stocks · up 2 / down 2 / flat 1 · sample mean +0.40%.
The top-ranked stock (NVDA) shows its previous close 140.00 and close 144.20. The template turns cents into dollars with row.close / scale.
NYSE has 2 stocks: JPM (flat) and KO (down). Mean -1.00%.
Stop the server.

sample4_sqlite.summary: An app that validates the CSV, stores it in SQLite in one transaction and draws the page from the database. Before flask --app app init-db imports the data there is no database and the page answers 500; edits to the CSV appear only after another import; and an invalid CSV does not erase the existing data.
steps: instance/market.sqlite3 does not exist yet. read_quotes() opens it with mode=ro, so instead of creating an empty database it fails, and the page answers 500 with a hint.
A command registered with @app.cli.command('init-db'). It validates the CSV, and import_snapshot() fills the quotes table in one transaction: Imported 5 quotes.
Query the stored rows directly. Codes are stored as TEXT, so leading zeros such as 000660 are kept.
Start the server on port 5004. The page now reads the database, not the CSV.
Sample mean +0.40% — the same data as sample2, so the same result.
Changing Samsung Electronics' close to 77000 in the CSV leaves the page at +0.40%, because the page reads the database.
After another import the change shows: Samsung's change goes from +2% to +10%, so the mean becomes +2.00%.
Appending a copy of a stock's row fails validation (duplicate code). Validation runs before the DELETE and the import is one transaction, so the database keeps the previous 5 stocks.
Stop the server. Reloading the page restores the CSV and the database.
